statements.text: Every request to a `/tasks` route — `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{id}`, `POST /tasks`, `PUT /tasks/{id}`, `DELETE /tasks/{id}` — must present a valid API key in the `X-Api-Key` request header.
A request to a `/tasks` route with a **missing** `X-Api-Key` header is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
A request to a `/tasks` route with an **incorrect** `X-Api-Key` header value is rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
The valid API key is the string value of configuration key `ApiKey`.
When the `ApiKey` configuration value is not set, the valid API key defaults to the literal string `test-secret-key`.

The API-key check runs before existence and payload-validation checks: an unauthenticated request for an unknown task id returns 401 (not 404), and an unauthenticated `POST /tasks` with a blank title returns 401 (not 400).
A rejected request reads no task and mutates no task: after an unauthenticated `DELETE /tasks/{id}` the task is still retrievable with a valid key.
The root health endpoint `GET /` stays public and returns 200 with no `X-Api-Key` header.
CRUD behaviour for authenticated callers is unchanged: the five pre-existing integration tests still pass once they supply the key, with the same status codes and payload shapes.
`dotnet build` and `dotnet test` stay green (R-003), `Domain/**` references no ASP.NET type (R-004), and the `TaskState` naming is unchanged (R-005).
